name: Attica — Athena, Poseidon, Cecrops, Olive, Sea, Verdict, and the Remembered Counter-Claim
description: The whole relational image: claim and witness, verdict and flood, variant aftermaths, the sanctuary that remembers both claims, the ratified toroidal reading and olive chain, and the verdict returned to the place.

scenes.name: Claim, witness, verdict
scenes.character: Poseidon strikes the middle of the Acropolis; Athena calls Cecrops to witness and plants the olive; Zeus separates; the twelve arbiters award the country on Cecrops's testimony; the city is named Athens.

entities.name: Cecrops — earth-born, man and serpent; the land already named Cecropia
Poseidon's trident — the sea called Erechtheis at the Acropolis's middle
Athena's olive — planted under witness
Zeus separates; the twelve gods arbitrate; Cecrops's testimony is the stated ground
Athens — named after Athena

text.title: Claim, witness, verdict
text.italic: The sequence demonstrates adjudication with its parts held apart: the divine arbiters are distinct from the king's witnessing, and the testimony to the planting is the award's stated ground.

text.body: Cecrops, son of the soil compounded of man and serpent, has already named the country Cecropia. Poseidon arrives first and strikes the middle of the Acropolis with his trident, producing the sea called Erechtheis. Athena arrives, calls Cecrops to witness her taking possession, and plants an olive. Zeus separates them and appoints the twelve gods; the country is awarded to Athena on Cecrops's testimony, and she names the city Athens.
Occurrences: Cecrops's naming and double nature (#0–#1); the trident-strike and Erechtheis (#1); the witnessed planting (#1, #4); the twelve arbiters and testimony (#1); the naming of Athens (#1).

scenes.name: The flood and its variant aftermaths
scenes.character: Poseidon floods the Thriasian plain; Hyginus has Mercury prevent the inundation; Augustine's Varro-derived telling takes the women's votes and the maternal names away.

entities.name: the flood — the Thriasian plain under the sea
Hyginus, Fab. 164 — Mercury, on Jupiter's orders, prevents the inundation
Augustine, Civ. Dei 18.9 — the women outvote the men, then lose votes, maternal names, and the designation Athenian
the Parthenon west pediment — the monumental contest, 437–432 BCE

text.kicker: #2 · Hyginus, Fabulae 164; Augustine, City of God 18.9; the Acropolis Museum's pediment record
text.title: The flood and its variant aftermaths
text.italic: The variants demonstrate the aftermath differing while the retained-contrary relation holds — no mythic action is asserted as established history.

text.body: The verdict does not dissolve Poseidon's force: he floods the Thriasian plain and lays Attica under the sea. Hyginus: Mercury prevents the inundation on Jupiter's orders, and Minerva founds Athens. Augustine: the women's vote chooses Minerva; the appeasement takes back votes, maternal names, the name Athenian. The west pediment gives the contest its monumental image, its trident-action readable as withdrawal or as striking to flood.
Occurrences: the Thriasian flood (#1, #2); the prevented inundation (#2); the women's vote and its removal (#2); the pediment's double reading (#2).

scenes.name: The sanctuary remembers both claims
scenes.character: The Erechtheion houses Athena's eastern room and Poseidon-Erechtheus below; the olive, the trident marks and the salt spring stand in the sacred centre; the burnt shoot regrows.

entities.name: the Erechtheion — Athena east; Poseidon-Erechtheus west, lower
the sacred olive — burnt, a shoot about a cubit by the next day (Herodotus 8.55); two cubits in Pausanias
the trident mark in the bedrock; the sea-water cistern sounding in a south wind (Pausanias 1.26.5–7)

text.kicker: #2 · Herodotus 8.55; Pausanias 1.26.5–7 and 1.27.2; the Acropolis Museum's Erechtheion account
text.title: The sanctuary remembers both claims
text.italic: The material relation demonstrates the retained contrary: the victorious civic form keeps the counter-claim inside its sacred architecture.

text.body: The Erechtheion's eastern room was Athena's; its lower western room housed shrines including Poseidon-Erechtheus. Herodotus reports olive and sea as the gods' witnesses, and the burnt olive's regrowth — a shoot about a cubit by the next day. Pausanias gives the altars, the cistern whose wave sounds in a south wind, the trident mark, and a two-cubit regrowth — a distinct report. The oil-fed lamp stays a separate cultic object.
Occurrences: the double shrine (#2); the olive's burning and regrowth in two reports (#2); the trident mark and salt spring (#2); the lamp kept distinct (#2).

scenes.name: The ratified reading: the well at the centre; the olive chain
scenes.character: The civic-rational order organised around an opening it cannot convert into itself; root → tree → fruit → pressing → oil → anointing → flame; a valid verdict is not an exhaustive ontology.

entities.name: the toroidal civic image — Athena's order wound around Poseidon's unfilled depth
the well/sea at the centre — archaic, mobile, retained, not abolished
the olive chain — root, tree, fruit, pressing, oil, anointing, flame/light
"the verdict determines the city; it does not exhaust the place"

text.kicker: #3 · the five ratified relations (all human-amplified: yes); A24; the Arbitration field
text.title: The ratified reading: the well at the centre; the olive chain
text.italic: The toroidal appointment embodies the theorem: the condition of the whole may remain present without becoming one more positive content of the governing form — wholeness through relation to an interior depth, not its filling.

text.body: Poseidon's well/sea is the archaic-magical depth enshrined within the heart of Athena's rational-civic form — toroidal, not linear: the formed city organised around an opening it cannot convert into itself. The olive chain runs root, tree, fruit, pressing, oil, anointing, flame — the gift through which Athena's claim is witnessed and made civic. Hybris begins when the achieved determination claims what it did not choose never belonged to the field.
Occurrences: the well at the centre (#1, #3); the olive under witness and its chain (#1, #3); the flood as retained force (#2, #3); the verdict's bounded authority (#1, #3).

text.title: The verdict returns to the place
text.italic: The whole returns-to A24 with the distinction a decision that binds from the claim that its result exhausts the place — the five unratified candidates kept visible without canonisation.

text.body: The whole returns-to A24: a verdict with real competence whose consequence remains within a larger field — retaining Poseidon's sign does not revoke Athena's award. The Arbitration field qualifies the return: Continuity-in-Indeterminacy, Criterion-through-Distinction, Arbitration-in-Crisis, Con-text-through-Diaphaneity, Resolution-in-Reconciliation. Athena's name becomes the civic noun; Poseidon's continued force shows the noun does not exhaust the place. The five candidate readings remain deliberately human-amplified: no, presented for encounter rather than installed.
Occurrences: the retained contrary in the sanctuary (#2, #5→0); the verdict and its bounded authority (#1, #5→0); the candidates held unratified (#5→0).
